title.narrative: Output 1.1. Increased institutional capacity of employer and business membership organizations (EBMOs)

description.narrative: The Employers Confederation of Zimbabwe (EMCOZ), in collaboration with the Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions (ZCTU) and the Zimbabwe Federation of Trade Unions (ZFTU), established a partnership to adopt a Joint Action Plan and sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) aimed at strengthening bipartite social dialogue. The primary focus was on jointly formulating policies for poverty reduction and employment creation, with emphasis on the formalization of the economy. Leveraging insights from the 2019 Zimbabwe Enabling Environment for Sustainable Enterprises (EESE) Report, EMCOZ identified priorities and policy actions designed to unlock the private sector’s potential as a catalyst for productivity growth, sustainable development, decent employment creation and formalization. These priorities were presented by EMCOZ at a high-level meeting organized in Harare on in Nov 2022 bringing together 50 representatives of employers and workers. Following the discussion, the EMCOZ, ZCTU and ZFTU developed and adopted a Joint Action Plan capturing a mutually agreed matrix of policy issues. They adopted recommendations for promoting rights at work including freedom of association, reinvigorating the national social dialogue institution and mechanisms, strengthening the social protection system and addressing the structural barriers in the informal economy. Subsequently, EMCOZ uploaded the matrix of policy issues to its website and widely circulated amongst the members. At their meeting with the President of Zimbabwe on 7 July 2023, the social partners discussed amongst other issues, their joint policy recommendations. Following the President’s guidance, the partners presented the policy recommendations at the meeting of the Tripartite Negotiation Forum (TNF) on 12 July 2023. Subsequently, TNF is monitoring the implementation of these policy recommendations through its subsequent meetings. The ILO provided technical support to EMCOZ by helping them identify, contextualise, and formulate the policy issues that are of concern to employers as well as workers. Additionally, the ILO offered oversight in the formulation of the agenda for the bipartite dialogue and ensured the quality of the final Matrix of Mutual Policy Issues. The ILO also developed the scope of work for the expert who facilitated the dialogue while providing coordination support for its organization. Importantly, the ILO built the capacity of EMCOZ by working closely with the EMCOZ Executive Director to refine the policy issues as well as professionalising the Memorandum of Understanding that was subsequently signed on 9 Dec 2022 . Many of these issues stemmed from the 2019 EESE report. Finally, the ILO guided EMCOZ Executive Director on how to communicate to its wider membership and to government, the importance of the bipartite partnership and the significance of key policy issues that were prioritised.
